author: Pedini
text:
tinkerbelle wrote: hi guys
thanks for reply what i dont get is term "origin of the move/origin" and
 why FTR is more important then "origin". i dont even know how to write
it properly but what is origin?, i mean 99% of swing highs/lows are
reactions on FTR on some timeframe (for example B on our chart)-->
then we break ((2) opposite ftr) and after break make new FTR (3) so how
 i understant charts there are only FTRs - origin is usualy reaction on
FTR (xyz) if we then break oposite FTR (2) and make FTR in direction of
break (3) ... it make sense for me and work pretty well! but why is
FTR(3) more imprtant than "origin/B/xyz FTR" is it only becouse it is
"fresh/untested" ? becouse if you think about these moves in terms of
orders there should be more orders from origin(need to break (2) ) then
on makeing FTR

and continue on this move higher... hope someone will get what iam trying to say :D... thanks and take care

The best advice i can give you is this. Find all the FTRs you can and
mark them out, see how price reacts when they are reached. How does
price arrive at the FTR? Does it break the FTR? If it does break what
happens next?

Origins are not as important and should be looked at as left over orders
 where price can react to. All the decisions happen at FTRs.

Peds
